---
title: "How misskappa Is Validated"
---

The estimators are checked at three levels. The checks live in the package's
test suite and the C++ unit tests, and they run on every change.

## Parity with established software

On complete data, the Conger, Fleiss, and Brennan-Prediger estimates and their
variances match the `irrCAC` package (Gwet 2019) on a raw-ratings example and
a counts-format example (nominal weights). The `irrCAC` values are frozen in
the test suite, so the check runs without `irrCAC` installed.

For scored ratings, the normal-theory FIML mean and covariance agree with the
saturated estimator in `lavaan`. This comparison runs whenever `lavaan` is
installed.

## Independent reference implementations

The normal-theory FIML fit and its sandwich covariance are compared with a
separate pure-R implementation kept in the test suite: an EM for the saturated
Gaussian mean and covariance, analytic casewise scores, and a
finite-difference observed information. The analytic gradients that map the
fitted moments to the coefficients are checked against numerical derivatives.

The C++ unit tests freeze values from the package's original implementation
and check known special cases. Two raters with complete nominal ratings
reproduce Cohen's kappa, perfect agreement gives a coefficient of one, the
available-case, IPW, and Gwet estimators coincide on complete data, and every
estimated covariance matrix is symmetric and positive semidefinite.

## Internal consistency of the inference

Every estimator returns per-subject influence rows `fit$psi`, and the tests
check the identity

$$
\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}}(\widehat\theta) = \frac{1}{n^2}\,\psi^\top\psi
$$

for each of them. The equality tests, joint covariances, and custom contrasts
all rest on this identity.

## What the tests do not cover

Consistency under MCAR and MAR, standard-error calibration, and interval
coverage are statistical properties of the estimators, not of the code. They
are studied by simulation in the companion methods papers (in preparation).

## References

Gwet, K. L. (2019). irrCAC: Computing chance-corrected agreement coefficients
among raters. R package.
